correctness.rationale: For n≥5 the dual has 5n tetrahedra corresponding to 4n coordinate squares plus n meridian C4 caps, no five-vertex faces. Removing two simplicial pairs per square and one per 4n unique-common-neighbor diagonals gives 14n elementary collapses and leaves square filling plus 8n(n−3) long edges. The square filling is a torus capped along n parallel meridians, hence S1∨nS2. An integral cellular 2-cycle has four equal square coefficients λ_b in each strip and cap coefficients λ_{b−1}−λ_b, uniquely ∑λ_b z_b; no 3-cell introduces a relation. Orientation of annuli and caps gives the stated signed dihedral generator action, and Alexander duality yields H_{4n−5}=Z^n and H_{4n−4}=Z^{8n(n−3)+1}. n=4 excluded.
